D010-D005_h001.question_both:
It’s been a weird year. About seven months back I just sort of went flat inside. I’d drive the cab, pick people up, drop them off, and feel nothing. Things I used to enjoy on my days off – football on TV, going for a drink with mates – I just stopped caring. Even small stuff, like choosing what to eat or what shirt to wear, feels like this huge decision now. I just stare at the menu or my wardrobe and can’t make up my mind. My ex says I’m like a robot with our son, like I’m there but switched off.

Then, about two months ago, it flipped. I’ve been on edge, snapping at passengers over nothing, shouting if someone hesitates getting in the car. I can’t sit still at the taxi rank – I’m pacing, tapping the steering wheel, walking circles around the car. When I talk, it’s like my mouth runs ahead of my brain; people tell me to slow down because they can’t keep up.

I’ve also been spending money like crazy – new stereo, clothes, online stuff I don’t need – my account’s a mess and my ex is furious. Lately I keep feeling like radio songs or people’s comments are secretly about me, like there’s some message. And sometimes when I’m driving, I get this crawling, buzzing feeling on my skin, like insects moving under my shirt, but there’s nothing there when I check.
D010-D005_h001.question_a:
It’s kind of hard to explain, but for about two months I’ve been on this…high, I guess, but not in a good way. I’m constantly on edge, snapping at passengers over tiny things—like if they’re slow with the seatbelt, I feel like exploding. I can’t sit still; even when I’m off shift I’m pacing the flat, tapping my fingers, walking circles. When I talk, my words just tumble out. My dispatcher keeps telling me to slow down on the radio because no one can follow what I’m saying.

I’ve been driving extra hours, and when I get paid, I blow the money on stupid stuff—expensive gadgets, clothes I don’t need. My bank account is a mess, and my ex is furious because I’m behind on support.

Lately I feel like random things are aimed at me—the songs on the radio, people talking on the street—I’m convinced they’re about me. I also sometimes feel things crawling on my skin, like bugs, but there’s nothing there. That only started with this “amped up” period.

Before this, for about five months, I was the opposite—completely flat. I didn’t enjoy anything, not even seeing my kids. I’d stare at the wardrobe for ages, unable to decide what to wear, or sit at a diner and not manage to pick from the menu. It felt like I was empty inside, and it got so bad I could barely work.
D010-D005_h001.question_b:
It’s been going on for more than a year now, I think. The worst part is the voices and… sensations. Even when I’m alone in the cab, I feel like someone’s touching my arm or crawling on my skin, but there’s nothing there. The radio, the ads on the bus stops, even people crossing the street—I keep feeling like they’re sending me messages just for me, like they’re talking about me or warning me.

There was a period, maybe two months, when I was really wound up and snappy. Small things from passengers would set me off, I’d shout over nothing. I couldn’t sit still—pacing in my flat, fiddling with my hands, needing to keep driving even when I was exhausted. I’d talk so fast my dispatcher and my ex said they couldn’t follow me. I also started buying stuff online—gadgets, car parts—blew through my savings and ran up debt. That revved‑up phase has settled down now, but the weird beliefs and the feeling of being touched are still there.

Lately I feel… empty. I don’t enjoy driving, football, nothing. It’s like my feelings are switched off. Even choosing what to eat or what route to take feels overwhelming. I’ve missed a lot of work because of all this.

For about a couple of months over the summer, I felt like I was on overdrive. On set I was bouncing between three different shoots and rewriting scripts at 3 a.m., storyboarding whole seasons in one night, barely sleeping but not feeling tired. I’d talk so fast in meetings that producers would ask me to slow down, but my head was moving ahead of my mouth. My mood would flip in seconds—one minute I’d be on top of the world, convinced this was my “genius phase,” and the next I’d snap at my AD for the smallest thing. I drove way too fast between locations, did more coke than I’m proud of, hooked up recklessly. It felt like nothing could touch me…until it all kind of crashed.  

Since then—five months, maybe more—I’ve been mostly flat. Getting out of bed feels heavy. I stare at scripts and can’t push myself to start, my head feels full of fog.  

On top of that, I sometimes hear this voice, not mine, commenting on what I’m doing. And I keep feeling like this actress I worked with is secretly in love with me, sending me “messages” through her Instagram posts, even though I know that sounds off.

I’ve been out in the woods most days like always, but for the past couple of months I feel like I’m wound way too tight. It’s like I’ve got this motor running in me all the time. I’ll hike my patrol route, then instead of resting I start clearing brush, fixing fences, planning new projects for the station. I can’t sit still, and when I’m in the cabin I just pace and keep coming up with “great ideas.”

I catch myself snapping at people over nothing—other rangers, hikers, even on the radio. Little things set me off: someone walking off-trail, paperwork not done just right, and I’m suddenly barking at them.

I’ve also been talking a lot more. Once I start, I just go on and on—about new tourism programs, buying extra land, opening some kind of wilderness retreat. I already put money into a couple of online “eco-investments” without really checking them out, more than I can afford on my salary.

There’s this woman from the regional office—I’m sure she’s been sending me signals, like special meaning in her emails, like she cares for me. And when I’m alone at night, I hear voices sometimes, like people talking just outside the cabin or calling my name, but when I go out, there’s no one there.
D010-D005_h006.question_a:
It really started about two months ago. I’m usually pretty even-keeled out in the woods, but lately I’ve been snapping over nothing. A hiker steps off the trail or a coworker is five minutes late, and I just blow up. I feel like there’s this motor running inside me all the time. I’m pacing the cabin at night, hiking extra patrols during the day, barely sleeping but not feeling tired. I can’t sit still long enough to read or watch TV.

I’ve been talking nonstop, too. My son keeps telling me, “Dad, slow down,” but once I get going about new projects or ideas, I can’t shut up. I’ve even put a big chunk of my savings into this online “eco‑tourism startup” without really checking if it’s legit. It felt like a brilliant move in the moment.

The strangest part is I’m convinced the new district supervisor is secretly in love with me—like she’s sending me hidden messages in emails and her tone of voice. Sometimes at night, when I’m wired and pacing, I hear her voice, clear as day, calling my name or telling me we’re meant to be, even though no one’s there. All of this has been going on together these past two months and has really messed with my work and my life.
D010-D005_h006.question_b:
It started a little over three years ago. The part that really scared me wasn’t the “high” spell; it’s how the voices and strange ideas never really left afterward.

About two years back I had this stretch, maybe two months, where I was just… wound up all the time. I’d snap at the younger guys over nothing, like if they left a gate unlatched I’d blow up. I couldn’t sit still in the lookout tower; I’d pace the catwalk half the night, full of this buzzing energy, like my body was plugged into a generator. I talked nonstop on the radio and to whoever would listen, barely letting them get a word in.

During that time I got it into my head to pour my savings into this online “eco‑tourism” thing a stranger pitched me. I didn’t really read anything, just wired the money. That wiped out most of what I had.

What hasn’t gone away are the voices and the ideas. Even when my mood settled back down, I keep hearing these men whispering my name in the trees, commenting on what I’m doing. And I’m still convinced the new district supervisor is secretly in love with me—little things she says I take as secret messages—though she’s never said anything like that outright. These thoughts and the voices have been there pretty steadily, even when I’m not revved up or irritable.

It’s been about two months now where I’ve felt like I’m running on some kind of internal battery that never runs out. I wake up after a few hours of sleep feeling wired, almost high on my own thoughts. My husband keeps telling me to sit down, but I just can’t—I’m pacing around the apartment, reorganizing things at 3 a.m., pitching three different story ideas to my editor in one email, talking so fast he has to tell me to slow down.

I feel…brilliant, invincible almost. I’ve been driving way too fast between interviews, weaving through traffic because it feels like I can react to everything before it happens. I’ve also started experimenting with stuff I normally wouldn’t touch—some pills a friend offered “just to stay sharp” on deadline. I didn’t really think about what could go wrong.

At the same time, I’ve become convinced people are watching me. When I’m out reporting, I notice the same car behind me for blocks, or I’m sure my emails are being tracked. I keep smelling this strange chemical, like burnt plastic or cleaning fluid, even when no one else notices it. I can’t tell if I’m just being paranoid or if something is actually happening, but it’s making it harder to focus on my work and my family.
D010-D005_h007.question_a:
For about the last two months, it’s like I’ve been “turned up” way past normal. I wake up after three, maybe four hours of sleep feeling wired, like I’ve had ten coffees. I’m buzzing with ideas for articles, side projects, even a book series, all at once. I can’t sit still; I pace around the apartment, reorganize things at 3 a.m., then start drafting whole features in one sitting, talking out loud as I type. My husband says I barely pause to breathe when I’m talking—I’ll jump from story pitches to politics to some “big plan” about exposing corruption, all in this rapid-fire way.

I’ve been driving way too fast to chase “leads,” convinced people are following me or reading my emails—like my editor and maybe even the government are tracking me. Sometimes I smell this sharp, chemical odor, like burning plastic, when no one else does, and I take it as proof they’ve bugged the apartment. But all of that—the fear of being watched, the weird smells—only started when this high, revved-up feeling began, and it hasn’t happened to me outside of this intense “on” phase. It’s gotten bad enough that I’ve missed deadlines and my editor pulled me off a big story.
D010-D005_h007.question_b:
I’m a reporter, so I’m used to questioning things, but for about a year now I feel like I’m the one being investigated. I’m convinced my editors and even people at other outlets are tracking me—through my phone, my laptop, even the TV. I’ll be at home with my husband and suddenly be sure there are microphones in the light fixtures. I try to tell myself it’s irrational, but it feels absolutely real in the moment.

I also keep smelling this strange chemical, like burning plastic or something medicinal, usually when I’m alone at my desk or in bed. My husband never smells it, even when I insist it’s really strong.

About ten months ago there was a stretch of maybe six to eight weeks where I was unnaturally “up.” I barely slept, had endless energy, was talking nonstop in the newsroom, pitching wild stories, driving way too fast between interviews. I even blew a lot of money on equipment I didn’t need. That high phase ended—my mood and energy dropped back to my usual baseline—but the sense of being watched and those weird smells have just kept going, every week, regardless of how my mood is.

D010-D005_h019.question_both:
I’m a guide at the museum, so I’m used to talking a lot, but this was…different. About three weeks in the spring, it felt like someone flipped a switch. I was constantly on edge, snapping at visitors for tiny things, arguing with coworkers over details I’d normally ignore. I couldn’t sit still—I'd pace the galleries before opening, reorganize labels that didn’t need it. My husband said I was talking “like a runaway train,” jumping from one idea to the next so fast he couldn’t follow or get a word in. I barely slept but didn’t feel tired then. It got disruptive enough that my supervisor asked me to take some time off.

Since then, it’s gone the other way and stayed that way for about seven months. I feel weighed down and empty most days. I don’t enjoy the art anymore, which scares me; it all looks flat, pointless. Nights are long—I lie there for hours before I can fall asleep. I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up, though I’m not planning anything.

Sometimes I’m convinced something terrible is coming, like the world’s unraveling. Other times I feel a crawling, tingling sensation on my skin, like something brushing past me, but there’s nothing there.
D010-D005_h019.question_a:
It really started about seven months ago. I just sank. I’d go to the museum, stand in front of a painting I normally love, and feel absolutely nothing. I’ve been down, kind of…gray, most days since then. I can’t enjoy anything—tours, books, even time with my husband just feels flat. At night I lie there for hours, staring at the ceiling, wishing I’d just drift off and not have to wake up. I don’t make plans to hurt myself, but the idea of just…not existing anymore sounds like a relief. It’s made it hard to keep up at work and at home.

Then about three weeks ago everything suddenly flipped. I got this rush of energy, like I was plugged into a socket. I hardly sit still, I’m reorganizing exhibits in my head at 3 a.m., snapping at my husband over nothing. I talk so fast in tours people look confused, but I can’t slow down. And lately I’m convinced something terrible is coming—like the world is about to end. Sometimes it feels like things are crawling just under my skin, brushing against me when nothing’s there. Those strange beliefs and sensations only started with this “up” spell; they weren’t there during the long low period.
D010-D005_h019.question_b:
It’s hard to piece it all together, but this really started about seven months ago. I just sank. I go to the museum and walk visitors through these gorgeous paintings, but I feel absolutely nothing. It’s like someone turned the color off inside me. I’m sad all the time, heavy, and I keep thinking it might be easier if I just didn’t wake up one morning, though I haven’t made any plans.

Nights are awful. I lie there for hours, my mind grinding, unable to fall asleep. Even on days off, I just sit in the kitchen, staring, not wanting to do anything I used to enjoy—no concerts, no reading, nothing.

About three months into that, I had this three‑week spell where I was oddly revved up and short‑fused. I was snapping at my husband over tiny things, pacing constantly, talking so fast on tours that people could barely follow me. But that passed.

What hasn’t passed are these…beliefs and sensations. I’m convinced something catastrophic is coming, like the world is winding down, and I feel these crawling, touching sensations on my skin when no one is near me. Those haven’t let up, even after that wired, irritable period ended.

I’ve been driving the school bus for over 20 years, so I’m used to early mornings and a routine. But for about seven months now, I’ve felt like I’m moving through mud. I wake up at 3 or 4 a.m., stare at the ceiling, and can’t fall back asleep. I don’t enjoy anything anymore—kids waving at me, talking to coworkers, even seeing my grandkids—it all feels flat. I’m just…sad all the time. On the worst days, I catch myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, though I haven’t made any plans.

Before this long low stretch, there was this three‑week period where I felt the exact opposite. I barely slept, but I was bursting with energy, pacing around the house, doing five things at once. I talked so fast my daughter kept telling me to slow down, but my thoughts were racing ahead. I was convinced I’d been chosen for something important, like I had some special role or power. Around that time and sometimes since, I’ve felt odd sensations on my skin, like bugs crawling or someone brushing past me when no one is there. It’s been hard to do my job and keep it together through all this.
D010-D005_h020.question_a:
It kind of feels like I’ve been living two different lives this past year.

About eight months ago I crashed hard. Since my wife died, I’d been sad on and off, but this was different. For the last seven months I’ve been down almost every day. I don’t enjoy anything anymore, not even watching the kids joke around on the bus. I used to love their energy. Now it’s like everything is gray. I wake up at three or four in the morning, wide awake, and just lie there thinking how pointless the day is. I’ve had a lot of thoughts that it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, but I haven’t planned anything.

Before that, though—about three weeks straight—it was the opposite. I was on top of the world. I barely slept and still felt wired. I couldn’t sit still; I was pacing the house, starting projects, calling the school at odd hours with “big ideas.” I was talking so fast my daughter told me she couldn’t follow me. I was convinced I was chosen for something huge, like I was meant to lead some national safety program for all the school buses, like the government would call me any day. Around that time I also started feeling things crawling on my arms and legs, like little bugs, even though nothing was there. Those weird sensations and those big beliefs only happened during that high period; once that ended and I sank into this long low stretch, they went away. I’ve barely been able to work since then.
D010-D005_h020.question_b:
It’s been about seven months now that I’ve been really down. I used to enjoy driving the kids to school, joking with them, but now I feel flat, like nothing matters. I don’t get any pleasure out of anything—TV, talking to my daughter on the phone, even my grandkids. I wake up at 3 or 4 in the morning, every day, and just lie there, heavy, thinking it might be easier if I wasn’t here. I keep thinking about death, not planning anything, but wishing it would just stop.

About five months ago, for around three weeks, I suddenly swung the other way. I felt on top of the world, like I’d been chosen for something special. I was talking nonstop, pacing around the house, couldn’t sit still, making big plans about starting some kind of “transport ministry.” I was supposed to be driving the bus, but I was too wound up and had to take time off.

What worries me is that even after that “high” ended and the depression came back, I still feel things crawling on my skin, like invisible hands touching me, and I’m convinced I’ve got some kind of special power or mission, even though I know it sounds strange.
